title: DNA data storage write throughput
bottleneck: DNA stores data at extraordinary density with millennia-long stability, but writing (synthesis) is slow, expensive, and error-prone: current throughput is bytes-to-kilobytes per second at dollars per megabyte, many orders of magnitude from archival-storage economics. Random access requires PCR-based addressing schemes that don't scale cleanly, and read latency is hours.
why_it_blocks: Global data growth will outrun conventional archival media on cost and footprint; DNA could be the ultimate cold-storage medium, but only if write speed and cost improve by 6+ orders of magnitude. Without that, it stays a demo technology.
current_state: Enzymatic synthesis and nanopore sequencing are driving costs down, with megabyte-scale demos achieved. Throughput and cost are still far from tape competitiveness. Random access remains slow because addressing specific strands needs sequencing-adjacent biochemistry rather than electronic row decoders.
